before.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves (Direct-Injection M260) Causing Rough Idle and Power Loss
before.description: Like other Mercedes direct-injected turbo engines, the M260 in the GLB (and the 1.3L M282 in the GLB 180/200) accumulates carbon deposits on the intake valves and intake tract over time because fuel is injected directly into the cylinder and never washes the back of the valves. This leads to unstable idle, hesitation, reduced power and worse fuel economy as mileage climbs, and German sources note the 1.3L can also develop coked injectors. It is a wear/maintenance issue, not a recall.
before.solution: Periodic walnut-blasting / intake valve cleaning resolves the deposits; some owners use quality top-tier fuel and occasional intake cleaners as mitigation. Keeping up with oil changes using MB-approved oil reduces oil-vapor contribution from the PCV system. Walnut-blast cleaning typically costs roughly 300-600 USD depending on shop.

proposal.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves (Direct-Injection M260) Causing Rough Idle and Power Loss
proposal.description: The reviewed Mercedes-Benz GLB manufacturer-communication and recall corpus does not establish the frozen carbon-buildup identity across M260 and M282 engines. Direct injection by itself is not evidence of excessive intake-valve deposits, a shared 2020-2024 defect, the stored progression or a universal cleaning interval. The U.S. corpus also does not establish the frozen GLB 180 and GLB 200 market applicability. Absence from this corpus is not proof that deposits cannot occur; exact market- and engine-specific Mercedes evidence is required.
proposal.solution: Preserve fault codes and fuel-trim, compression, leakage and misfire data. Check ignition, injection, air leaks, software and mechanical sealing before inspecting intake deposits with a borescope. Do not buy a walnut-blasting service, intake cleaner, valve, injector or cylinder head from this page; neither the cause nor a universal retail remedy is established.
symptoms: ignition, fueling, sealing and deposits separated

before.title: Emergency Call (eCall) System Disabled by Communication Module SIM Software Error (Recall 22V365)
before.description: An error in the communication module's embedded SIM-card software can cause a loss of mobile-network connection on GLB-Class vehicles, which disables the automatic emergency call (eCall / Mercedes me emergency) function. In a crash the vehicle may fail to automatically alert emergency services, and connected services may stop working. This is relevant in the EU where eCall is mandated. Covered by NHTSA recall 22V365 (Mercedes campaign spanning 2017-2022 GLB and other models).
before.solution: Under recall 22V365 the communication module software is updated, either over-the-air or at the dealer, at no charge. Owners should confirm Mercedes me emergency call is functional and have the software campaign performed if it shows as open for their VIN.

before.description: Certain 2021 GLB 250 vehicles can have a damaged Electronic Stability Program (ESP) control unit. A damaged ESP unit can disable the anti-lock brakes (ABS) and electronic stability control (ESC) and can cause an electrical short circuit, increasing crash and fire risk. before.solution: Under recall 22V679 the ESP unit is inspected and replaced as needed at no charge. If ABS, ESP or brake warning lights appear, stop relying on those systems and have the vehicle diagnosed; confirm the recall has been completed via VIN lookup.

before.title: Front Axle Carrier (Integral Carrier) Corrosion / Failure (Recall 21V990)
before.description: On certain 2020 GLB 250 vehicles, the integral carrier that supports the front axle may corrode, which can cause it to fail. A failure of the front axle carrier can compromise steering and suspension integrity and increase the risk of a crash. This is covered by NHTSA recall 21V990 and is part of a broader Mercedes campaign that also touched related A220 and AMG GLB35 models for front-axle corrosion protection.
before.solution: Under recall 21V990, dealers inspect the front axle carrier and replace it if corrosion is found, free of charge. Owners in road-salt/EU winter regions should verify the campaign has been completed and report any clunks, vibration, or steering looseness for inspection.

before.title: M260 Cylinder Head Exhaust Valve Seat/Guide Wear (Misfires, Compression Loss)
before.description: The 2.0L turbo M260 four-cylinder used in the GLB 250 / GLB 35 (and the M264-related variants) suffers from premature wear of the exhaust valve seats and valve guides. The exhaust valves stop sealing, causing loss of compression in one or more cylinders, rough running and misfires. Mercedes acknowledged this as a manufacturing defect and issued a voluntary extended warranty in the US and Canada covering cylinder head replacement for up to 15 years / 150,000 miles on affected 2019-2022 A-Class, CLA, GLA and GLB vehicles. A 2026 NHTSA-posted TSB (MC-11028267) documents the valve seat/guide wear on M260/M264 engines. Left unaddressed it can progress to catastrophic piston/secondary damage that is NOT covered by the warranty extension.
before.solution: Have misfire/rough-idle symptoms diagnosed promptly; the cylinder head is replaced under the 15yr/150k extended warranty if the VIN qualifies. Use only Mercedes-approved oil (MB 229.x) and premium fuel, and address any P030x misfire codes immediately to avoid uncovered piston damage. Out-of-warranty cylinder head replacement typically runs into thousands of dollars in parts and labor.
symptoms: Compression loss in one or more cylinders

Do not buy a cylinder head, valves, guides or timing parts from this page; coverage and parts must be determined by VIN.

before.title: Water Intrusion Into Front Footwells Causing Blank Instrument Cluster or Engine Stall (Recall 20V246)
before.description: Certain early 2020 GLB 250 4MATIC bodies were not sealed properly during manufacturing, allowing water to enter through the front wheel-well area into the front-occupant footwells. The water can reach and damage electrical components, resulting in the instrument cluster going blank or the engine stalling while driving with an inability to restart. NHTSA recall 20V246 (MBUSA campaign 2020070009) covers approximately 5,680 vehicles; the recall began July 31, 2020.
before.solution: Under recall 20V246, the dealer seals the body in the wheel-well area and inspects the front footwells for water intrusion, repairing damaged components at no charge. Owners should check their VIN at NHTSA/MBUSA and have the campaign performed if not already completed; watch for wet front carpets, which indicate intrusion.

before.title: 8G-DCT Transmission Shudder
before.description: The 8G-DCT dual-clutch transmission exhibits shudder and hesitation during low-speed maneuvers and from a standstill. While improved over the earlier 7G-DCT, the 8G-DCT still uses a wet clutch design that can judder when the clutch packs wear or the software calibration is outdated.
before.solution: Update the TCU software to the latest calibration. A transmission fluid change can improve clutch engagement feel. In persistent cases, the clutch assembly may need replacement under warranty.
